newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate panel approves Albright nomination.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate panel approves Albright nomination.

text.p: Madeleine Albright, chosen to be the first female U.S. secretary of state, easily passed her first test on Monday when the Senate Foreign Relations Committee unanimously recommended her confirmation.

The panel voted 18-0 to support her appointment and send it to the Senate floor for final approval. Committee aides said the full Senate was likely to vote on Wednesday to confirm Albright's nomination to succeed Warren Christopher, who held the job during President Bill Clinton's first term of office.

The committee voted without debate at a brief meeting shortly before Clinton arrived at the Capitol for his inauguration to a second term. Albright, currently U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, has seen her nomination speed through. She was the first member of Clinton's new Cabinet whose appointment has been acted upon by a Senate committee.

The committee last week held a confirmation hearing that was largely a love feast in which senators praised her selection and cited her as a role model for women and for those who seek the "American Dream."
Albright, 59, was born in Prague and immigrated to the United States with her family at the age of 11, fleeing Nazism and communism after the Second World War.

Before being named to the U.N. post, she taught international relations at Georgetown University, headed a Democratic Party think tank and advised unsuccessful Democratic presidential contenders Walter Mondale and Michael Dukakis. She also worked for former President Jimmy Carter and former Sen. Edmund Muskie.
Christopher's resignation as secretary of state took effect on Monday, when he was due to head home to California after Clinton's inauguration.

If confirmed as expected, Albright likely would be sworn in on Thursday. In the interim, Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott, who is staying on in that position at least temporarily, will be secretary of state ad interim.
Once in office, Albright was expected to announce her new State Department team, which sources say will include many members of the staff that served her at the United Nations.
There is speculation U.S. Ambassador to Russia Thomas Pickering, one of America's most senior diplomats, could be named to the No. 3 position as undersecretary of state for political affairs.

Two close aides, Elaine Shocas and James Rubin, were to receive senior positions. Shocas was expected to be named chief of staff and Rubin assistant secretary of state for public affairs, although Christopher's spokesman, Nicholas Burns, was expected to remain in that job for several months.
U.S. officials said Albright was considering making her first overseas trip on Feb. 12 through 22, travelling to world capitals in Europe and Asia.
